This vignette shows a few reusable simulation helpers: predator–prey dynamics (Lotka–Volterra), Beta–Binomial posterior predictive draws, and a simple linear DAG with post‑treatment bias.

## Setup

```{r}
library(tidyrethinking)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

## 1. Predator–prey dynamics (Lotka–Volterra)

```{r}
sim <- simulate_lynx_hare(
  n_steps = 500,
  init    = c(10, 20),
  theta   = c(0.5, 0.05, 0.025, 0.5),
  dt      = 0.01
)

sim |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(L, H), names_to = "species", values_to = "abundance") |>
  ggplot(aes(step, abundance, color = species)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) + theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Predator–prey dynamics", x = "time step", y = "abundance")
```

## 2. Beta–Binomial posterior predictive draws

```{r}
pp <- simulate_beta_binomial(n_draws = 2000, size = 9, alpha = 7, beta = 4)
pp |>
  ggplot(aes(x = w)) + geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, center = 0.5, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  labs(title = "Posterior predictive counts", x = "successes", y = "frequency") + theme_minimal()
```

## 3. Linear DAG with post‑treatment bias

```{r}
d <- simulate_bad_controls_post_treatment(n = 2000, bXZ = 1, bZY = 1, seed = 1)
GGally::ggpairs(d) # if GGally available; otherwise scatterplots:
```

```{r}
if (rlang::is_installed("GGally")) {
  GGally::ggpairs(d)
} else {
  d |>
    tidyr::pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "var", values_to = "val") |>
    ggplot(aes(var, val)) + geom_violin(fill = "grey70") + theme_minimal()
}
```
